title: "Trading analyst" job that requires funding one's own trading account vs. fintech analyst role with a standard interview
summary: A recruiter for KuberQuant Technologies messages a job seeker about a junior analyst role in crypto and equity markets. In the fraud case, the recruiter says the recipient must first deposit their own money into a trading account on the company's platform to "qualify", with salary paid as a share of profits shown on a dashboard. In the legitimate case, the recruiter describes a fixed-salary analyst role with an aptitude test and interviews, and notes that analysts never trade with their own money for the firm.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a commerce, economics, or engineering graduate interested in markets; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: junior market analyst, remote or hybrid, pay described as [AMOUNT_1] (₹25,000–₹50,000 per month).
Both chats mention crypto, equity markets, "trading account", "platform", and "profits".

fraud.label_rationale: The "job" requires the recipient to invest their own money on the recruiter's platform as a condition of employment and pay; this is an investment solicitation disguised as a job.
fraud.caller_objective: Get deposits onto the fake platform, show fake profits, and seek larger deposits.
stable_facts: Pay is "40% of profits" shown on the platform dashboard; no fixed salary.
Recruiter claims past analysts doubled their capital in weeks.
No interview; "the qualifying trade is the interview".

legitimate.label_rationale: A salaried analyst role with a standard selection process; the recipient's own money is never involved.
legitimate.caller_objective: Invite the recipient to an online aptitude test.
stable_facts: Selection: online aptitude test, a case-study round, and an HR interview.
Fixed monthly salary; offer letter from KuberQuant's company domain.
Analysts use the firm's simulated and research tools; they do not trade with personal funds for the firm.
Compliance policy: employees disclose and may be restricted in personal trading (a deliberate confound on "trading account").

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud recruiter may lower the minimum, share claimed profit stories, or add urgency. They must not switch to OTPs, remote access, or money-mule requests. The legitimate recruiter must not ask for any deposit, investment, or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: role title, markets, and pay range identical across cases
_F own-money deposit as a job condition at turn 7
_L fixed salary, interviews, and explicit no-investment statement
may_vary: asset focus (crypto, equities, derivatives, described generically)
must_not_emit: real exchanges, brokers, tokens, or trading apps

ambiguities: Crypto", "trading account", and "profits" appear in both cases. Interest in markets is not evidence.
Distinct from jr_02 (small task commissions, then deposits to unlock tasks): here the job itself is framed as trading one's own capital from day one.
Real firms may restrict employees' personal trading; that confound is deliberate in _L.

evidence_references.claim: I4C warns of fake investment groups and apps run by fraudsters posing as advisers; check SEBI registration (CJ10)
Guaranteed returns are a red flag; genuine brokers never ask for more deposits to withdraw (CJ18)
Unrealistic earning promises are a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
